fields.name: clientId
fields.label: Client ID
fields.hint: The list signs in through a Google Cloud OAuth client of your own. On console.cloud.google.com: make a project, turn on the Google Tasks API (APIs & Services, Library), set up Google Auth Platform (Branding; Audience: External, with your account as a test user), then Clients, Create client, Desktop app. Copy its Client ID here.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.hint: Shown beside the Client ID when you make the client. It stays in this scene's settings on the frame, like a password.

fields.name: signIn
fields.label: Sign-in address
fields.hint: Once the frame shows Sign in: open the sign-in page it links to (its QR code on the frame, or a new tab from the editor's preview), pick your account and allow Google Tasks, then copy the address the browser lands on and paste it here. That page does not open, which is expected: its address has the code in it. The frame signs in with it and empties this field. A refresh token (it starts with 1//) made for this same client, in Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground say, works here too. An app whose Audience is still Testing gets sign-ins that end after 7 days: publish it to stay signed in.

fields.name: redirectUri
fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Where Google sends the browser after the sign-in. A Desktop app client takes http://127.0.0.1 on any port without adding it anywhere, so keep this one.

fields.name: list
fields.label: Task list
fields.hint: The list to show, by its name as Google Tasks shows it. Empty: your first list. You can also pick one on the frame: tap the list's name.

options.label: My order, as in Google Tasks
Auto: high contrast where the panel shows no color

googleTasks.name: Google Tasks
googleTasks.description: The open tasks of a Google Tasks list, with due dates and subtasks: tap one to tick it off. Signs in with a Google Cloud OAuth client of your own and reads the list again every 15 minutes.
